messages:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — scheduling a maintenance sweep in az3 to reduce egress queue pressure and cool down GPU hosts. This will be a rolling drain + node reboot flow. Window: 2026-04-02 02:00–06:00 UTC. Expected impact: transient 5–12% GPU capacity loss on az3, short tail-latency blips on some routes. Details below.

SRE-Bot: Scheduled maintenance created: MDT-az3-egress-20260402. Notifying oncall.

Maria Gomez: Timeline looks OK from our side. Which racks/nodes are in scope? Can we avoid touching Dedicated reserved pools if possible?

Alex Chen: Starting with racks r-az3-06 -> r-az3-10. Sequence: stateless inference nodes first -> pooled dedicated -> pinned Dedicated last. We'll pre-warm fallback endpoints in eu-west and us-west prior to live traffic shifts. Plan: drain nodes one at a time, apply egress QoS tweak, allow GPUs to cool, then reboot if temp >78C.

Jia Patel: Can you paste the exact run commands and the QoS bits? I'll automate but want to review flags.

Alex Chen: Yes — steps we will run from the runbook. Example drain commands: 
```bash
kubectl cordon $NODE
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30
```
QoS sample (we apply via config agent):
```bash
# reduce egress burst for inference-heavy hosts
tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root tbf rate 800mbit burst 32k latency 400ms
```
Automation script path: /ops/scripts/az3_qos_sweep.sh — script will iterate nodes, apply tc, run short canary, then reboot if temperatures are high.

Noah Rivera: Heads-up that several Dedicated customers have SLA clauses. I recommend we proactively route their traffic to reserved pools in us-west while we touch their hosts, and include them in notifications.

Maria Gomez: I'll coordinate CS email drafts — do we want 2h pre-notify + at-start + post-complete?

Ops Oncall: I can own the rollback hook and incident posts. Rollback commands: 
```bash
tc qdisc del dev eth0 root || true
kubectl uncordon $NODE
```
I'll also monitor grafana panel: infra->egress_queue_occupancy and infra->gpu_temp_by_pod.

SRE-Bot: Canary test scheduled: canary-az3-001. After first 2 nodes we'll run 5 small inference jobs.

SRE-Bot: Canary result for canary-az3-001: avg latency +2.1%, p95 +4ms, errors 0/500 — PASS.

Alex Chen: Good. Execution cadence: runbook will attempt ~6 nodes/hour. Estimated finish ~2026-04-02 04:45 UTC for the first wave. Abort criteria: any Dedicated pool observes >3% error increase or sustained p99 increase >50ms. @Noah @Maria please confirm comms cadence. :warning:

Noah Rivera: Confirmed. I'll send 2h pre-notify and an in-progress at start; will escalate to account owners if we hit any Dedicated impacts.

Maria Gomez: Drafted message, pinging Legal for wording. Will paste the final shortly. :thumbsup:

Ops Oncall: Posting runbook and will post live updates in #incidents. Pager for this window: Jia.

Jia Patel: I'll run the automation and watch the logs. One thing — for pods protected by PDBs, do we want to honor PDBs or force eviction? I prefer honoring PDBs and skipping nodes that block unless we hit emergency.

Alex Chen: Agree. Use --grace-period 30 and respect PDBs; if PDB blocks, mark node for manual migration and continue. We'll only force if incident.

SRE-Bot: Event log snapshot:
[2026-04-02T01:12:00Z] maintenance scheduled by Alex Chen
[2026-04-02T02:00:07Z] canary started (canary-az3-001)
[2026-04-02T02:12:35Z] canary passed

Maria Gomez: Notifying product for potential UX impacts.

Alex Chen: Thanks team. Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/ops/az3_qos_sweep — I'll update this thread with any deviations.

Noah Rivera: Copy, standing by to trigger customer routes.

Ops Oncall: I'll post status updates every 30m in #incidents and escalate if we hit abort criteria.

Jia Patel: Starting automation in ~5m for the canary run, I'll report back with the execution log snippet.

Alex Chen: Appreciated. :rocket:
